title: Sticky burst retention gap during allocation rebalancing causing sustained 429s
creator: Ava Martinez
description: High-severity customer escalations reported intermittent, sustained 429s during multi-region allocation rebalancing and tenant failover. The symptoms point to a gap in how the allocation rebalancer migrates the tenant's burst token ledger and lease epoch across hosts when a node is preempted or when requests are rerouted from Dedicated -> Hosted. This ticket tracks diagnosis, short-term mitigations, and the permanent fix for ledger handoff correctness and reconciliation to prevent token undercounting that results in opaque throttles.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a tenant on Dedicated pool with active burst credits (simulate sustained low-latency traffic that consumes credits).
2) Trigger allocation rebalancer by simulating node preemption / scale-down on the host carrying the tenant ledger, or force-orchestrator to reassign the tenant to another host,
3) Concurrently generate a short burst of traffic from the same tenant while the handoff is in-flight,
4) Observe immediate 429s and rapid credit depletion on the receiving host; ledger inspection shows epoch mismatch or missing commit for outstanding tokens.
root_cause: Allocation rebalancer performs a fast lease handoff but does not fully persist in-flight burst ledger deltas before the recipient host begins admission. In the narrow interleaving, recipient reads an incremented lease epoch without the last delta, causing it to apply conservative undercounts and immediately reject requests. The problem is exacerbated when fallback routing switches traffic between Dedicated and Hosted planes with different reconciliation semantics, leaving transient orphaned credit deltas.
impact: High. Multiple enterprise customers on Dedicated pools experienced sustained 429s for 3-20 minutes during rebalancer events and orchestrator failovers. Customer success escalations received from Acme Analytics (dc-17) and NovaDocs (dc-22). Client applications saw error loops and degraded user experience. Risk of SLA breach for Dedicated contracts and increased support load.
mitigation: Applied immediate protective change: block allocation rebalancer preemption for tenants with >50% active burst credits (hotfix deployed 2026-03-12),
Added temporary admission guard: recipient host now queries donor ledger snapshot TTL and stalls admit for 2s if snapshot not confirmed (reduces race surface),
Customer success: contact list and status updates sent to impacted customers; traffic reroutes and manual credit restores applied for highest-severity tenants.
proposed_fix: Implement a two-phase handoff for burst ledger deltas: (1) donor flushes pending delta batch and writes a durable handoff marker; (2) recipient polls for the marker and performs idempotent apply of deltas, then acknowledges. Also add a reconciliation job on tenants rebalanced in the last 10 minutes to reconcile token counts and auto-heal discrepancies. Update admission logic to use monotonic ledger version + signature to avoid conservative undercounting.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge and code review of implementation (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/1024),
2) Canary rollout to non-production and a small set of Dedicated clusters (dc-stage, dc-canary),
3) Monitor reconciliation metrics and 429 rate for 24 hours,
4) Gradual rollout to all Dedicated pools with feature flag default-off, enable per-tenant after validation,
5) Backfill reconciliation for tenants that experienced the handoff race in last 72 hours.
qa_plan: Unit tests for ledger flush + handoff marker semantics,
Deterministic integration test that injects preemption during in-flight delta commit (CI harness),
Chaos test: run rebalancer while traffic generator produces burst pattern to validate no regression,
Load test in staging at production-like QPS to measure latency SLO impact of extra handoff step
monitoring: Alert: sustained tenant 429 rate > 1% for 5m in Dedicated pools -> P0 pager,
Dashboards: per-tenant token-epoch drift and reconciliation success rate (console link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/burst-reconciliation)
comments: 2026-03-11 - Ava Martinez: Initial triage. Customer reports trace show 1s rebalancer event then immediate 429s. Flagged as P0 and paged SRE. Captured heap snapshots and admission logs for affected hosts.
2026-03-12 - Ravi Patel: Deployed hotfix to block rebalancer preemption for hot tenants. Short-term change reduced customer 429s on dc-17; still saw a residual window on one cluster (dc-22).
2026-03-12 - Mei Chen (SRE): Added admission stall guard (2s) as temporary mitigation; observing drop in handoff-induced 429 spikes in canary. Monitoring configured and runbook updated.

2026-03-13 - Jordan Lee (PM): CS notified impacted customers. We committed to a fix that avoids prolonged manual credit restores. Linked customer compensations and SLA remediation plan to this ticket.
2026-03-14 - Ravi Patel: Submitted implementation PR for two-phase ledger handoff and reconciliation job. Requesting review from storage and orchestrator teams. Opening e2e tests in CI.
2026-03-14 - Security (Anika Rao): Reviewed design surface; no immediate secrets exposure. Recommending a short security sign-off before full rollout to production.
